ingredients.name: Oyster or button mushrooms
ingredients.notes: oyster mushrooms are preferred for best texture and flavour; cremini or portobello work well too; cut into large pieces or tear by hand

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: diced; adds acidity and body to the gravy

ingredients.name: Thick coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 1/2 cup; added at the end; do not boil vigorously

steps.instruction: Clean the mushrooms by wiping with a damp cloth -- do not rinse under running water as mushrooms absorb moisture and will steam rather than fry. Tear or cut into large pieces.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let splutter. Add fenugreek, curry leaves, and pandan leaf. Sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, and green chillies. Saute for 3-4 minutes until the onion softens and turns golden.
Add turmeric, chilli powder, and curry powder. Stir for 30 seconds to toast the spices.

Add the mushrooms and diced tomato. Toss to coat in the spice base. The mushrooms will release their moisture -- cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 minutes until the moisture evaporates and the mushrooms begin to brown at the edges.
Pour in the thin coconut milk and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 8-10 minutes.

Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir gently and simmer uncovered on low heat for 2-3 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly. Do not boil vigorously. Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice or roti.

source_site: theflavorbender.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, foodcnr.com, rasakama.wordpress.com, borntobespicy.com, easypeasycurry.com, and srilankancuisine.org
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; strong agreement on the temper-then-simmer technique and the importance of not rinsing mushrooms under water
notes: Mushroom curry is a widely beloved vegan and vegetarian dish that multiple Sri Lankan food bloggers describe as one of the best meat substitutes in the cuisine, alongside jackfruit curry (sl_019) and cashew curry (sl_018). Oyster mushrooms are consistently preferred across sources for their meaty, chewy texture and ability to absorb curry flavours; button or cremini mushrooms are common substitutes. Not rinsing mushrooms in water is a technique point consistently repeated -- mushrooms absorb water readily and will steam in the pan rather than developing the slightly browned, flavour-concentrated edges that make this curry its best. The curry tastes even better the next day as the mushrooms continue absorbing the spiced coconut milk.
